chain.label: NMSP mission-first culture and absent safety/risk-assessment policies
chain.trigger: the NMSP aviation section did not have an SMS program... no requirement for a risk assessment at any point during the mission; inadequate pilot staffing; lack of an effective fatigue management program

chain.label: pilot fatigue from restricted, fragmented sleep and a long duty day
chain.trigger: the pilot was still experiencing some residual fatigue on the day of the accident... he had accumulated 11 hours 41 minutes of duty time and 4 hours 30 minutes of flight time in the previous 24 hours

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's PIO duties prevented him from obtaining sufficient rest, and NMSP policies did not ensure protected rest periods for its pilots

chain.label: no helicopter instrument rating or inadvertent-IMC training
chain.trigger: the accident pilot did not have a helicopter instrument rating, experience in helicopter instrument operations, or training specific to inadvertent helicopter IMC encounters

caused_by.evidence: aviation section helicopter pilots were not required to have a helicopter instrument rating because of cost constraints and mission requirements

chain.label: remote 11,600-ft ridge landing site surrounded by high rugged terrain
chain.trigger: the remote landing site was surrounded by high, rugged terrain that was no longer visible

chain.label: dark moonless overcast night with no ground lights
chain.trigger: the night of the accident was particularly dark, with no moonlight... the sky was overcast, minimizing starlight, and there were no ground lights in the remote area

chain.label: strong gusty westerly winds and mountain turbulence
chain.trigger: the spotter opened his door, felt very strong, cold westerly winds... the helicopter encountered strong winds and turbulence below 200 feet agl

chain.label: weather deteriorated to IMC over the landing site and departure path
chain.trigger: the sleet had turned to snow, and the clouds had lowered... IMC prevailed when the helicopter departed the remote landing site about 2132

chain.label: self-induced pressure to complete the rescue and situational stress
chain.trigger: the pilot was experiencing increased situational stress as a result of the perceived challenge posed by the deteriorating conditions... significant self-induced pressure for him to ensure that the mission was successfully completed

caused_by.evidence: 'It's going to start snowing up here and if it does that, I've got to get the [expletive] out of here'... 'I'm not going to spend a lot of time or we're going to have two search and rescues'

chain.label: pilot's decision to take off from the remote site into dark night IMC
chain.trigger: the probable cause of this accident was the pilot's decision to take off from a remote, mountainous landing site in dark (moonless) night, windy, instrument meteorological conditions

caused_by.evidence: even rudimentary consideration of the adverse weather conditions should have indicated to the pilot that it was no longer safe to take off
fixation on a course of action... while disregarding critical evidence that the course of action is no longer safe is also consistent with the effects of fatigue
the 'tunnel vision' created by acute situational stress caused the pilot to fixate on the goal of taking off from the remote landing site as soon as possible
the lack of such a risk assessment allowed the decision-making errors that manifested themselves in this accident situation to occur
taking off in a helicopter in dark (moonless) lighting conditions, with marginal visibility... poses an unacceptably high risk
the spotter stated that the strong wind continued to blow while the pilot was recovering the hiker

chain.label: loss of outside visual references and spatial/geographic disorientation after liftoff
chain.trigger: almost immediately after takeoff, the helicopter was in the clouds with 'zero visibility' and... the flight was very turbulent

caused_by.evidence: the pilot took off and began to maneuver the helicopter in the direction that he had pointed
the low clouds and snow likely obscured the mountains and led to an inadvertent IMC encounter shortly after takeoff
he was not prepared to react appropriately to the loss of visual references that he encountered shortly after takeoff
multiple risk factors for spatial disorientation... maneuvering in dark night conditions, and turbulence, were present during the accident flight

chain.label: erratic flightpath, tail strike on the mountainside, and inability to control the helicopter
chain.trigger: the helicopter began to fly erratically... the pilot stated, 'I struck a mountainside. [I'm] going down'

caused_by.evidence: he could not tell exactly how the helicopter maneuvered because he could not see anything outside; it seemed as if the pilot was struggling to control the helicopter
the helicopter crossed terrain as high as 12,500 feet before descending rapidly near the crash site

chain.label: impact with terrain at 11,970 ft and roll down a steep rocky slope
chain.trigger: the helicopter impacted terrain for the second time at an elevation of 11,970 feet... After the second impact, the helicopter rolled down a steep, rock-covered slope

caused_by.evidence: descending rapidly near the crash site... near the top of a steep ridgeline

chain.label: pilot and hiker ejected and fatally injured; spotter seriously injured
chain.trigger: the commercial pilot and one passenger were fatally injured; a highway patrol officer who was acting as a spotter during the accident flight was seriously injured

caused_by.evidence: during this descent, components of the helicopter separated from the fuselage, and the pilot and hiker were ejected
neither the airborne nor ground SAR personnel could have reached the pilot before he died of exposure given the adverse weather conditions... the rugged terrain... the distance they had to travel
